evidence: The survivors exploit that levels are binary and that the required sum is the number of bonds: qwen notes “Since r_u...” after “The constraint is sum of (r_u - r_v)^2 = m”, while deepseek and gpt-oss immediately build BFS 2-colorings.
affordance_in_statement: A tuning configuration assigns each monomer a resonance level, which must be chosen as either 1 or 2. ... the total energy ... must be exactly equal to m: $$ \sum_{i=1}^{m} (r_{u_i} - r_{v_i})^2 = m $$
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: with values restricted to 1 or 2, every squared difference is intrinsically 0 or 1, so equality with the number of bonds intrinsically means every bond joins differently assigned monomers. It can only be re-presented indirectly through an equivalent physical energy model, but that will not remove the underlying reduction.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that every edge must have different endpoint levels and uses BFS bipartite coloring.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: levels “must be chosen as either 1 or 2” and the energy is “exactly equal to m”

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses component-wise BFS 2-coloring, with component orientation chosen to satisfy lexicographic minimality.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the squared-difference sum has m terms and is required to equal m

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly reduces the constraint to checking that every recorded bond has unequal endpoint levels, then tests bipartiteness.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: # The constraint is sum of (r_u - r_v)^2 = m

common_affordance: Because each endpoint level is 1 or 2, every bond contributes at most 1 to the energy, and requiring the sum of m contributions to equal m forces every bond to contribute 1; the task is therefore exactly bipartite graph coloring plus lexicographic orientation.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The attempted approach uses degree information and does not establish the required canonical component orientation by the smallest-index vertex, so its coloring can fail the lexicographically smallest tie-break even when the graph is bipartite.

recommended_edit: No single semantics-preserving edit can defeat all survivors: the shared shortcut is the intrinsic mathematical structure of the task, not incidental wording. Defeating it would require changing an immutable core element, such as allowing additional resonance levels or changing the energy target.
